methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic information units based on individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This ensures a granular comparison between the two sets of information.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Lemmings can be modeled using a finite state machine.
Lemmings can be in walk_left state (walk_left = 1).
Lemmings can be in walk_right state (walk_right = 1).
Lemmings switch direction when bumped.
If bumped on the left (bump_left=1), Lemming walks right.
If bumped on the right (bump_right=1), Lemming walks left.
If bumped on both sides, Lemming switches direction.
When ground=0, Lemming falls and aaah=1.
When ground=1 after falling, Lemming resumes walking in the same direction.
Bumping while falling does not affect walking direction.
Being bumped in the same cycle as ground disappears does not affect walking direction.
Being bumped when the ground reappears while still falling does not affect walking direction.
Lemmings can dig when dig=1.
Lemming can dig if ground=1 and not falling.
Lemming continues digging until ground=0.
When ground=0 after digging, Lemming falls and aaah=1.
Once ground reappears after digging, Lemming resumes walking in original direction.
Being bumped while digging has no effect.
dig input is ignored when falling or when there is no ground.
Falling has higher precedence than digging.
Digging has higher precedence than switching directions.
areset is positive edge triggered asynchronous reset.
areset resets the Lemming to walk left.
walk_left and walk_right indicate the direction of movement.
When walking left, walk_left=1 and walk_right=0.
When walking right, walk_left=0 and walk_right=1.
spec_atomic_units: walk_left, walk_right, aaah, and digging are determined by the current state and inputs.
Prioritize conditions in the order: falling, digging, direction switching.
aaah is asserted (1) when ground is 0 (aaah = !ground).
digging is asserted (1) when dig is 1 and ground is 1 (digging = ground & dig).
walk_left and walk_right indicate the direction the Lemming is walking.
Direction changes based on bump_left, bump_right, and dig input.
When ground is 0, Lemming continues walking in the same direction as before the fall.
When dig is asserted and ground is asserted, the Lemming starts digging.
Walking direction is irrelevant during digging until the Lemming falls.
When bump_left is asserted, the Lemming switches to walking right.
When bump_right is asserted, the Lemming switches to walking left.
If both bump_left and bump_right are asserted, the Lemming still switches direction.
walk_left and walk_right are mutually exclusive.
Direction switching logic can be implemented using XOR gates.
dig input and ground input must be considered to determine when the direction switching logic is active.
walk_left and walk_right are determined by the current state and bump inputs, but only when the Lemming is not falling or digging.
Only one of walk_left or walk_right is asserted at any given time.
next_direction = current_direction ^ (bump_left | bump_right)
walk_left = (!ground & !dig) & (!next_direction)
walk_right = (!ground & !dig) & (next_direction)
areset asynchronously resets the state machine to the walking left state on the positive edge.
The outputs walk_left, walk_right, aaah, and digging reflect the current state of the Lemming and are updated on the rising edge of clk.
The state transitions occur on the rising edge of the clk signal.
The state updates are likely implemented using non-blocking assignments (`<=`) within an `always @(posedge clk or posedge areset)` block.
